name: 50411-imageprefill-qwen2vl2b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
architecture: Qwen2VLForConditionalGeneration, bf16, ~2.2B: a native-resolution 32-layer ViT (patch 14, spatial merge 2) over a ~1.5B Qwen2 decoder, 32768-token context. A 1280x720 image is not downscaled; it is 1196 image tokens.
load_profile: concurrent, streams=100, bounded at 100 requests with an 1800 s safety cap. One wave: 100 streams x 1 request each, so all 100 are issued at once and all 100 are scored. No warmup and no cooldown -- the arrival ramp of the wave is part of what is being measured, not something to discard.
workload: Single-turn image+text chat: one 1280x720 JPEG (quality 85, i.i.d. noise pixels, row-index seeded so every request carries different pixels) plus exactly 1024 tokens of synthetic text, output pinned to 1 token -- about 2240 prompt tokens per request. Driven in-process through guidellm's `vllm_python` backend rather than over HTTP, so the tokenizer's own chat template renders the image block.
purpose: A 2B moderation service giving one-token verdicts on 100 simultaneous posts, each pairing a 720p photo with a page of text, on one GPU.
launch:
# vLLM at commit 9c22668436a4d94aab87ea74a220e060415cf1d8 (`git describe --tags --match "v*"` =
# v0.26.1rc0-420-g9c22668436a4), on 1x H100 80GB HBM3. Any flag not listed is an engine default.

model: Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# Worst case on the wire is about 2240 prompt tokens plus 1 generated; 4096 clears it with room.
max-model-len: 4096

# Pinned, not tuned: these are the values `vllm serve` itself resolves to on a >=70 GiB non-A100
# card. They are spelled out because the engine is driven in-process here, and that context is not
# a key in the server's default table, so it silently falls through to the library floor of
# 2048/128 -- a quarter of the batch a served engine would use on this hardware.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024

error.text: the patched version's own code raises an error as the engine starts
